headline: Outside review of the district's hiring and personnel protocols, up to $30,000, approved.
summary: The superintendent said the reviewer will be chosen through a competitive process, and the district will cover the cost, though the funding source is not yet set. The superintendent hopes to finish the report by the end of winter, and findings will be presented at a future meeting with a public summary. Separately, the committee recommended that the City Council approve $23,547,692 for the Roberts accelerated repair program. Other votes approved a construction manager at risk plan for Missituk and Brooks elementary repairs, a school calendar policy change, and a press release backing the Medford High School project.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, 7-0, including bills, payrolls, an $18,815.17 donation, and two field trips.
Approved hiring an outside reviewer for district hiring and personnel protocols, up to $30,000, 7-0.
Recommended that the City Council approve $23,547,692 for the Roberts accelerated repair program, 7-0.
Approved construction manager at risk process for Missituk and Brooks elementary accelerated repairs.
Approved the first reading of a revised school year and school calendar policy (Policy IC).
Waived the second reading of the school calendar policy revision.
Approved a press release supporting the Medford High School project.
Approved a resolution asking the facilities and capital planning subcommittee to review district capital projects and update the plan.
discussion: Outside audit of hiring protocols: Members asked how a reviewer could access personnel files, and the superintendent said individual employee records would not be reviewed. The superintendent said a student stability plan item could be added, and the motion was amended to include changes from tonight's discussion.

Band program public comment: Parents who spoke during public comment said students were not checked in with after a recent departure, and asked that the audit review possible harm to students and communication with families.

Special education entry plan: Members asked when measurable targets would be set, and the assistant superintendent said the SEPAC would be active by January and the procedural manual revised by the end of the school year. Member Russo asked for a follow-up report on reading proficiency for students with IEPs.

MCAS results and gaps: Staff said math scale scores rose in five of six grades, with grade 6 holding at 493, and that grade 6 English exceeding-and-meeting was 14% against the state's 22%. Members asked about reading gaps and middle school results, and a member said they would send questions by email.
Roberts repair funding timing: The Roberts accelerated repair funding paper goes to the City Council on the 17th, and construction next year depends on the funding being in place.
